title: Courts in criminal cases
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:33Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point, leg-summary-indictable-offences, is an NSW card about classifying offences and uses the Local Court, not the Victorian three-tier court allocation (Magistrates', County and Supreme Courts) that this point needs, so it would require more than small changes.

draft.title: Courts in criminal cases
card: Criminal cases in Victoria are heard in different courts, depending on how serious the offence is.
hears summary offences, which are less serious, such as minor theft or some driving offences. It also handles early steps in more serious cases.
hears most indictable offences, which are serious offences such as armed robbery.
hears the most serious indictable offences, such as murder.
draft.remember: The more serious the offence, the higher the court that hears it.

a.q: Which court hears a trial for murder in Victoria?
a.why: Murder is among the most serious offences, so it is heard in the Supreme Court. The County Court hears most indictable offences, but not the most serious ones such as murder.
a.clue: Choose the court for the most serious cases.

b.q: Sam is charged with a minor summary offence of wilful damage to a bus shelter. Which court will most likely hear the case?
b.why: Summary offences are less serious and are heard in the Magistrates' Court. The County Court hears most indictable offences, which are more serious than this one.
b.clue: Minor offences go to the lowest court in the list.
